terminal_record.title: Israeli Deputy Foreign Minister Warns Iran War Could Resume
terminal_record.description_short: Sharren Haskel warned on June 23, 2026 that war with Iran was very likely unless the Iranian regime changed.
terminal_record.description_medium: Israel’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel warned on June 23, 2026, that war with Iran was “very probable” unless there was “a huge change within the regime.” Her remarks followed a U.S.–Iran memorandum intended to extend a tenuous ceasefire. Reuters reported Israel was not part of the negotiations. The sources establish a warning about the deal’s fragility, not an Israeli decision to restart fighting or a promise to do so within days.
terminal_record.description_long: On June 23, 2026, Israel’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel told a Jerusalem press briefing attended by news.com.au that renewed war with Iran was “very probable” unless there was “a huge change within the regime.” She also said, “We are at a very dangerous point right now.” Her remarks came after the United States and Iran announced a memorandum intended to extend a tenuous ceasefire and open talks toward a permanent truce. Reuters reported that Israel had not participated in the negotiations and that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had distanced Israel from the agreement, leaving uncertainty about whether the ceasefire would hold. The reporting supports a warning about the fragile agreement, not evidence that Israel had decided to restart fighting or promised to do so within days. The frozen record’s claims about unnamed officials, Iranian provocations, and weaknesses in Trump’s framework are not established by the accessed reports and are omitted. Its Associated Press link concerns a separate Gaza dispute and does not support this Iran entry.

terminal_record.title: Unverified Claim of February Arrest Threats Against Milley and Esper
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges February 2025 arrest threats against Mark Milley and Mark Esper; the cited material does not establish them.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump and senior White House officials threatened in February 2025 to arrest and prosecute Mark Milley and Mark Esper over criticism. The supplied AP citation concerns different actions against Milley: a security-detail and clearance revocation and an inspector-general review. It does not document the alleged arrest threat or establish a matching threat against Esper. Keep the allegation attributed and internal pending direct evidence.
terminal_record.description_long: The supplied record alleges that in February 2025 Donald Trump and senior White House officials threatened to arrest and prosecute former officials Mark Milley and Mark Esper because they had criticized Trump. It says the two had described Trump as dangerous and unfit for command, and characterizes the alleged threats as an effort to silence critics and warn other officials against speaking publicly. The record also says Milley and Esper stated they would not be intimidated. These statements remain allegations in the supplied record; the materials do not verify the threats, the attributed comments, or the claimed chilling effect. The cited Associated Press excerpt documents a separate January 29 action: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revoked Milley’s security detail and clearance and ordered a Pentagon inspector-general review. That report does not establish an arrest threat and says nothing here about a matching threat against Esper. This internal draft keeps the allegations attributed and publication ineligible pending direct, event-specific evidence.

terminal_record.title: Supplied March 15 Claim That Trump Called the Judiciary ‘Rigged’ Remains Unverified
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied March 15 claim that Trump called the judiciary “rigged” is unverified; a March 14 transcript records narrower criticism of some judges.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump said on March 15, 2025 that the federal judiciary was “rigged against” him, but the packet does not verify that date or wording. It also links the claim to an appointment count and later rulings that are not supported here. An official transcript records different remarks on March 14 criticizing some judges.
terminal_record.description_long: The supplied record alleges that Donald Trump said on March 15, 2025 that the federal judiciary was “rigged against” him. The packet does not verify that date or wording. It also combines the alleged statement with a first-term appointment count and claims about rulings on later executive orders; those claims are not established in the supplied materials. An official transcript documents different remarks the previous day, March 14, when Trump criticized some judges while discussing officials at the Justice Department. That transcript is adjacent context and does not prove the March 15 statement or the broader claim about the entire judiciary. The supplied account therefore remains unverified as to its central event. No conclusion is drawn here about judicial appointments, particular rulings, or the motive for the alleged statement. Criticism of judges is not itself a factual finding that the judiciary is biased.
terminal_record.date_precision: day as supplied; exact statement date not verified
